about.heading: About
about.p1: I'm an architect and engineering leader with 21 years of taking systems from the first whiteboard sketch to production. Most recently I helped a major real estate company rethink how its developers work, bringing in AI tools like Claude and MCP servers, automated DevOps and earlier security checks. I built the tooling and trained its developers to use it.
about.p2: I'm good at getting different teams pulling in the same direction, setting standards that stick, and shaping how teams hire and test. I've worked in banking, real estate, marketing, logistics, procurement, government, healthcare and e-learning. I'm based in Salt Lake City and work in English and Spanish.

privacy.title: Privacy
p: When you ask for my resume on this site, I keep what you type: your name, email, company, role and, if you add it, how you found me. I also keep whether you checked “Rod may contact me”, and when.

I use it to give you the resume link and to check who is asking (see Lookups below). If you checked the box, I may also reach out to you about it. I don't use it for anything else, and it's never sold.

Everything is stored in my own database (Supabase). I don't keep your IP address; I keep only a salted hash of it to limit abuse. My hosting providers (GitHub and Supabase) may log it briefly for security.

I keep your request for 12 months if you checked “Rod may contact me”, and for 90 days if you didn't. Blocked or automated requests are kept for 90 days. If you checked the box, your name, email, company and role are also kept in my contacts so I can reach out. They stay there until you ask me to delete them (email {email}; I'll do it within 30 days). Copies of your request in backups are removed within 7 days after that.
To see or delete what I hold about you, email {email}. I'll answer within 30 days.
Cookies: none. If you pick a language, your browser remembers that choice (a setting called ds-lang, stored only on your device and never sent to me).
This site has no analytics, ads or third-party trackers, so it doesn't respond to Do Not Track signals; there's nothing to turn off.

azure.hosting: Everything is stored in my own database (Supabase). I don't keep your IP address; I keep only a salted hash of it to limit abuse. My hosting providers (Microsoft, through Azure Static Web Apps, and Supabase) may log it briefly for security.

lookups.heading: Lookups
lookups.intro: This is about the resume form. I'm Rod Johnson, and I'm responsible for it.

items.text: When you ask for the resume, I may look up your name, your company and the role on public sources, such as your company's website, public LinkedIn pages, public business records and search results. Automated tools and AI assistants may run these lookups for me.

Only to check that you and your company are real, for example a real recruiter or hiring company with a real role. My legal basis is my legitimate interest in checking a business contact. I may decide not to reply, or not to send the resume, based on what I find. Results can be wrong, and you can ask to see, correct or delete them.

I use only what is publicly visible, nothing private or behind access I'm not given. I don't use data-broker or people-search sites, and I don't buy data. No photos, face matching or reverse-image searches, and nothing about personal traits such as age, health, family, religion or politics. I look up only you and your company, once per request, with no re-checks and no profiles.

I record only a verdict (real, unclear or not found) and links to the public sources. I delete it 12 months after your request, or after 3 months if the check finds nothing or the request was spam. This verdict is kept longer than the other details you typed, which are deleted on the schedule above.
Never sold, and not shared with anyone else, except the services that store and process it for me (such as Supabase and the AI service I use), or when the law requires it.

lookups.rights: To see, correct or delete a lookup, or to object to it, email {email}. If you're in the EU or UK, you have the right to object to this lookup. If you'd rather not agree, you can't get the resume through this form, so email me and we can talk directly.

rvp.metaDescription: Twenty-seven questions about what you have, what you value and how you work. Your answers stay in your browser.
rvp.title: Which RVP archetype are you?
rvp.lede: RVP maps three things: the resources you draw on, the values that decide for you, and how you get things done. Twenty-seven short questions, about five minutes.
rvp.privacy: Your answers stay in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server. If you copy your result link, it carries your answers; a downloaded card stays on your device.
rvp.notClinical: A map, not a prison: for reflection, not a diagnosis. It is not a clinical test or a hiring tool, so please don't use it to label or screen other people. RVP is Rod's own framework, not a validated test.
rvp.homeBody: Twenty-seven short questions about what you have, what you value and how you work. Your answers stay in your browser.
